item.title: Mihara Castle & the Suigun Road: A Sea-Castle Ruin — Guide
item.description: Mihara Castle was built in the 1560s by Kobayakawa Takakage on islets in the sea, a naval stronghold so surrounded by water it was nicknamed the ‘floating castle’. Land reclamation has long since left it inland, and its keep is gone, but substantial stone ramparts and a moat survive — remarkably, right against Mihara’s shinkansen station, whose platforms were built over part of the site, making this possibly the most accessible castle ruin in Japan.
